title: BCI signal bandwidth vs thermal budget
bottleneck: High-bandwidth BCIs generate gigabits of raw neural data per second, but implanted electronics must stay within strict thermal limits (brain tissue tolerates ~1C rise, capping implants at tens of milliwatts). Amplifying, digitizing, and transmitting thousands of channels overheats tissue unless data is compressed or processed on-chip, which costs more power. Bandwidth and heat are fundamentally at odds.
why_it_blocks: The thermal ceiling caps how many neurons a BCI can ever record, limiting the richness of decoded intent. Physics, not engineering effort, sets the channel-count limit.
current_state: On-chip spike detection and compression reduce telemetry, and low-power ASICs stretch budgets. Thousand-channel wireless implants within thermal limits are the current frontier. Every microwatt spent on telemetry is a microwatt unavailable for recording, forcing lossy compression of the neural data itself.
